messages:
julia_cust: Hey team — onboarding FinOnboard (customer) with BYOK across AWS + Azure. During our integration test writes we hit 403/401s. AWS errors: "AccessDeniedException: The provided encryption context did not match" when calling GenerateDataKey. Azure returns 401 on wrapKey. Can someone advise on common misconfigurations?

maria_support: thanks — can you paste the exact error payload and the principal you're using (IAM role / managed identity)? Also which SDK/version?

julia_cust: sure — role is arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/finonboard-redwood. Azure uses a system-assigned MSI on our AKS pod (object id 5a1f...). Error snippets: `AccessDeniedException: The provided encryption context did not match` and `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized - code: Unauthorized - message: Access token does not have key unwrap permission`.

kevin_security: usually this is either an EncryptionContext mismatch or missing key-level permissions. For AWS: if you use an encryption context during generate, the same exact map must be provided during decrypt. For cross-account use you also need the KMS key policy to specifically allow the external principal or create a grant. For Azure: ensure the managed identity has key unwrap/wrap rights at the key scope (not just vault-level).

alex_eng: quick repro I ran locally: `aws kms generate-data-key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111:key/abcd --encryption-context Purpose=redwood,Customer=finonboard --query CiphertextBlob --output text | base64 --decode > dek.blob`. If the app later calls decrypt without the same `--encryption-context` map (same key names/case), AWS rejects with that exact message. Note: order doesn't matter, but key names/values are exact-match.

sara_prod: this points to a docs gap — our BYOK quickstart doesn't clearly show encryption-context usage for SDKs. I'll add explicit examples for AWS/GCP/Azure.

kms-bot: rotation_event: key arn:aws:kms:111111:key/abcd rotated at 1798456000 — check that the customer isn't still sending envelopes with the prior key version.

maria_support: @julia_cust can you pull last 5 CloudTrail events for `kms:GenerateDataKey` and paste the `encryptionContext` section? For Azure, run `az keyvault role assignment list --scope /keys/<key-name> --keyvault-name <vault>` and paste the result. RBAC propagation can take 2-5 minutes after assignment.

julia_cust: found the issue on AWS — our pipeline set `encryption-context` key as `Customer:FinOnboard` (capital F and different key name). After switching to `customer=finonboard` (lowercase), GenerateDataKey succeeded. Azure is still 401. We assigned `Key Vault Crypto User` to the MSI at the vault scope, but suspect we need key-scope assignment.

maria_support: for Azure you need role assignment on the key scope: e.g. `az keyvault role assignment create --role "Key Vault Crypto User" --assignee <msi-object-id> --scope /keys/<key-name> --keyvault-name <vault>` and confirm `key unwrapKey` is in `keyOps`. If the vault is using access policies (classic) vs RBAC there are subtle differences — check if vault has RBAC enabled.

kevin_security: also check the Key Vault's `Azure AD` condition: if the token audience or app id is mismatched the unwrap will 401. Confirm the AKS pod identity is exchanging token for `https://vault.azure.net` resource. If any prior failed decrypt attempts existed, we'll want to rotate the DEK and reissue envelopes after fix. I'll open a quick audit for failed decrypts.

alex_eng: sample AWS key policy snippet for cross-account (replace principals):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowUseFromFinOnboard",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/finonboard-redwood"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

sara_prod: filing docs PR now to include the encryption-context note + Azure key-scoped RBAC example + sample KMS key policy. Will link when done.

kms-bot: grant_event: grant id g-0a1b2c created for principal arn:aws:iam::222222222:role/finonboard-redwood at 1798456500.

maria_support: next steps for us: 1) customer fix encryption-context casing (done), 2) assign Azure key-scope role (customer to do), 3) confirm CloudTrail/Azure logs show successful Unwrap/GenerateDataKey, 4) if any DEKs were exposed rotate and rewrap. I'll create support ticket RED-8942 and mark P1 until write tests succeed.

julia_cust: thanks all — I'm applying the key-scoped role now. ETA ~10 mins. Any chance you can review RED-8942 when created?

sara_prod: I'll watch and review the ticket, will also push the docs PR in ~2 hours and post the link here. :thumbsup:

maria_support: thanks @julia_cust — ping once tests pass and we'll close the ticket. If Azure still 401 after role assignment, include the `WWW-Authenticate` header from the 401 response and we'll escalate to platform infra for token tracing.
